description: Argus is an open-source monitoring tool for servers and applications, with an AI investigator built in. You run it on your own infrastructure with one Docker command, then add its SDK to your apps. It watches metrics, containers and processes, and when something looks wrong it investigates: it correlates metrics, logs and events and explains the likely root cause in plain language. Free and MIT licensed; your data never leaves your servers. The landing page should send people to the GitHub repo and the docs.

reasons.surface: A dark surface matches the terminals, dashboards and GitHub pages your self-hosting audience already stares at all day.
reasons.display-type: IBM Plex Sans was made for technical products, so headings fit your servers and containers crowd and its even letters stay readable on dark grey.
reasons.body-type: Libre Baskerville is a serif built for long reading, so your plain-language root-cause explanations feel written by a person rather than dumped by a machine.

reasons.brand-color: Blue is the everyday colour of dev tools, so "View on GitHub" and link text read as familiar, and it sits far from your green, amber and red status dots.
reasons.secondary-color: Sticking to the brand colour and greys means nothing on the page competes with your links or your status dots.

reasons.neutral: Cool greys match the blue brand colour and the dark surface, so panels and text never look warm or muddy.
reasons.semantics: Green, amber and red are the colours people already read as success, warning and error, so your server and container states are understood at a glance.
reasons.spacing: Comfortable spacing on an 8px base puts more air between rows and sections, which makes your root-cause text easier to read, and it can drop to 4px inside dense metric tables.
reasons.radius: 4px corners are square rather than rounded, plain and technical like the GitHub repo and docs people land on.
